title: cross-functional roadmap sync prep - Dec 2025 - Asha notes
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Owner: Asha Patel (notes)
Date: 2025-12-10 10:00am PT (30m)
Location: Zoom / #roadmap-sync thread
Attendees (planned): Daniel Kim (PM), Maya Thompson (Eng lead), Rafael Ortega (Applied ML), Priya Singh (SRE), Asha Patel (Product ops)

Purpose / goals for this sync:
- Align around top Q1-2026 initiatives that affect serving/runtime, model onboarding, and product rollouts.
- Surface major risks/dependencies (infra capacity, quantization path, eval gating) and agree owners.
- Finalize phasing for Canary rollout + fallback policies for Hosted API.

Context / background (short):
- Product roadmap doc (Confluence) proposes piecewise rollout: "Model Catalog v2", "Predictive Batching", "Quality Monitoring/Evals". Some dates are optimistic given infra capacity and applied-ml bandwidth.
- Eng has two major delivery chunks: runtime kernels + autoscale policy changes (INFRA-76) scheduled in Jan-Feb.
- Applied ML needs 3 weeks per model for evaluation + quantization profiling before we mark variants as "canary-eligible".

Agenda (10m each topic):
1) Quick status round (5m) — PM / Eng / ML updates
2) Model Catalog v2 timing and gating (10m) — who signs off on canary? what level of eval coverage?
3) Predictive batching: infra constraints + rollout plan (10m)
4) Next steps + action items (5m)

Key questions I want to raise:
- What is the absolute earliest we can do a limited canary for Model Catalog v2 without risking customer regressions? (Maya/Rafael)
- Can ML reduce per-model eval time by parallelizing profiling across infra? (Rafael + Priya)
- If autoscaler changes are delayed, what fallback policy do we expose to customers? (Daniel + Maya)

Notes to self (things to call out verbally):
- Call out the "fallback policy" as product-facing: need decision on default (auto-fallback to smaller model / region-based routing).
- Emphasize that quantization profiles must be committed to model catalog entries and pinned per-version.
- Mention PROS/CONS of rolling canary per-customer vs per-route.

Draft alignment proposals (to present):
A. Model Catalog v2 rollout phases:
   - Phase 0 (internal preview): Dec 15 — internal teams + staging (no external traffic)
   - Phase 1 (canary per-route): Jan 20 — 5% traffic to canary variants for low-risk routes (search/rerank)
   - Phase 2 (broader canary): Feb 10 — expand to more routes and customer cohorts if error/quality metrics stable

B. Canary gating checklist (must-have before Phase 1):
   - Quantization profile completed and validated (applied-ml)
   - Evals: baseline prompt set pass rate >= X (TBD)
   - Runtime perf: latency regression < 5% on p50/p95 (eng perf)
   - Rollback path tested and documented

C. Predictive batching rollout approach:
   - Start with server-side simulated load tests (Priya) week of Jan 6
   - Toggle-on for low-latency routes with monitoring for token-level cost and p95 latency

Risks / blockers:
- Applied ML bandwidth: Rafael estimates 6 models queued for Jan; need 30% more hours to hit catalog v2 schedule.
- Infra capacity: GPU slots are constrained mid-Jan due to other customer migrations (see INFRA-76).
- Quality gating thresholds are not defined (we need to agree on "pass" thresholds for canary).

Action items (owner / due):
- Rafael: produce per-model quantization profile template + estimated TFLOPs cost (due 2025-12-18) [linked to GH PR #456].
- Maya: validate runtime perf tests for canary variants and add perf dashboards (due 2025-12-22) [Jira: PROD-128].
- Priya: schedule predictive-batching simulated load window and share test plan (due 2025-12-19) [Jira: INFRA-76].
- Daniel: draft customer-facing canary communications and rollback FAQ (due 2025-12-20).
- Asha (me): consolidate canary gating checklist and propose numeric thresholds for pass/fail (due 2025-12-17).

Follow-ups I want from the sync (explicit asks):
- Concrete estimate of applied-ml capacity (Rafael) in hours per model + who can be pulled in for profiling.
- A clear list of routes/features considered "low-risk" for initial canary. (Product)
- Confirmation from SRE on acceptable p95 latency increase during batching tests.

Unresolved questions to file in Confluence after meeting:
- Define "quality pass" threshold for generative features (TBD: 80% vs 90% on curated eval set).
- Which pricing/telemetry signals will we surface to customers when we enable predictive batching?

Slack/Links to mention in meeting:
- Roadmap thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1700000000000000
- PR for quantization templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRD/Cross-Functional+Roadmap+Sync+Q1-2026

Notes after last sync (quick):
- Daniel agreed to customer comms draft and will share a first cut by 12/13.
- Maya flagged a perf regression on long-context models; Eng will run a targeted perf pass this week.
- Rafael needs one extra quant engineer for 2 weeks in early Jan; flagged to people ops (email thread linked).

Next meeting: tentatively 2025-12-17 EOD (15m) for finalizing gating checklist.

Personal TODOs (post-meeting):
- Update Confluence with final checklist and attach this notes doc (Asha).
- Follow up with Rafael for the model priority list and share with Eng.
- Add PROD-128 and INFRA-76 links into the roadmap page for visibility.

-- end of notes --
